_doc: Move-purity manifest. Each target declares the original file and its replacement PARTS, where every part records the ORIGINAL LINE RANGE it covers. catdiff.js asserts: (A) each part's bytes equal the pristine original's bytes for that range, (B) the ranges tile 1..N with no gap or overlap, (C) concatenating them reproduces the whole original byte-for-byte, (D) for client targets, the <script src> order parsed out of the real 'orderFrom' file equals the parts' ascending line order, and (E) every part's current on-disk sha256 matches a pin in clientPins -- the recoverable guarantee for a part declared modified:true, mirroring serverdiff's [SE]. A part with modified:true is EXPECTED to fail (A)/(C) against pristine and is skipped there by design; (E) is what keeps it honest instead, re-pinned deliberately in the same commit as any intentional change. Order is derived from the real HTML, never trusted from this file -- a disagreement between the two is reported as the bug. Check [5] (scriptblock.js) additionally validates the script block itself.
_lineEndings: This repo has core.autocrlf=true: files are CRLF on disk, LF in git blobs (app.js is 891641 bytes on disk vs 874347 in the blob -- exactly one extra byte per line). RAW byte-identity is MANDATORY for client parts; CRLF->LF is used only as a failure diagnostic and can never produce a PASS.

FEATURE (requested): confirmDialog(msg, opts) gains optional yesLabel/noLabel/forceChoice, all defaulting to the existing behavior (Confirm/Cancel, X and backdrop both dismiss) so every EXISTING caller that just does confirmDialog(msg) is completely unaffected -- the labels are re-set on every call rather than left as static HTML, precisely so a later plain call cannot inherit a previous call's custom wording. forceChoice hides the x (#confirmCloseBtn) and makes the backdrop/x's shared window._dismissConfirmDialog() a no-op, so a prompt whose answer has to be a real decision -- keep or discard an autosaved Create Issue draft, the first and so far only caller -- cannot be dismissed by an accidental stray click. FEATURE: reported live -- a ticket created straight into the backlog (no sprint) and marked Done without ever being planned into a sprint used to sit in the live Backlog lane mixed in with real candidates for the next sprint, so dragging a batch of backlog items into a new sprint could silently pick up already-finished work. The Backlog lane's filter now excludes status='Done' (!iss.sprint_id && iss.status !== 'Done'); those issues get a separate 'Done (Not in a Sprint)' lane instead, placed between the live Backlog and the completed-sprints section. Given the exact same closed-lane treatment already established for completed sprints in this file: collapsed by default, no drop target, no 'Add issue' button -- it is a place to find these tickets, not a pool to plan the next sprint from. Cards stay draggable (backlogRow is unchanged), so deliberately dragging one into a real sprint for record-keeping still works. Verified against the real running app: a Done-no-sprint ticket does not appear in the live Backlog lane, does appear in the new lane (collapsed by default, no data-sprint-drop attribute), and a genuine To Do ticket is unaffected and still appears in the live Backlog lane exactly as before. || FEATURE (requested): bulk-move from the Backlog lane. Double-clicking a Backlog row (only the ungrouped Backlog lane -- sprint/Done-lane rows are untouched, see backlogRow's `selectable` flag) turns on checkboxes for every Backlog row and checks the double-clicked one; a plain click on any row then toggles its own checkbox instead of opening the issue while select mode is on. "Move to Active Sprint" and "Move to Sprint Planning" appear beside the Backlog header once select mode is active, moving every checked issue via the SAME per-issue PUT /api/issues/:id/move endpoint a single drag already used (Promise.all across the selected ids), so the server-side issue.move permission (member tier, not the stricter issue.bulk) and existing history/notification behavior are unchanged -- available to every space member, same as dragging one card already is. "Move to Sprint Planning" moves directly when there is exactly one planning sprint, or opens a small popup (styled like the MBR/Your Work header filters) to pick one when there is more than one. The checkbox itself overlays the row's own left padding rather than joining the existing 7-column grid, so turning select mode on/off never touches that grid. || FIX (reported live, "double-click just opens the ticket"): a real double-click always dispatches two 'click' events before 'dblclick' -- _blRowClick's very first click, while select mode was still off, called openIssuePage immediately and navigated away before 'dblclick' ever got a chance to turn select mode on, so double-clicking looked indistinguishable from a plain single click. The not-yet-in-select-mode branch now delays openIssuePage by 280ms in a cancellable timer; _blEnterSelectMode clears that pending timer before turning select mode on, so a genuine double-click never opens the ticket, while a genuine single click still opens it, just fractionally later. Also fixed in the same pass: .bl-row-checkbox had no default `display: none` -- the <input> is always in the DOM for every selectable row regardless of select mode (see backlogRow's own comment on why), so it was visible on every fresh page load instead of only once select mode is on; now gated under .backlog-row.bl-select-mode .bl-row-checkbox. || FEATURE (requested): extended the Backlog lane's bulk-move to the Active Sprint lane and every Planning Sprint lane too, so moving is possible in any direction among all three -- Backlog, Active, Planning -- not just out of the Backlog. Selection state moved from a single Backlog-only pair of globals to window._blSelect[laneKey] (laneKey is the real sprint id for an active/planning lane, or the literal string 'backlog'), kept independently per lane so checking tickets in one sprint doesn't affect another's selection; backlogRow's second parameter is now that laneKey instead of a plain selectable boolean. Each lane's own header swaps its normal Start/Complete/Edit/Delete buttons for the move toolbar while actively selecting (built by the new _blLaneToolbarHtml, shared by all three lane kinds), offering "Move to X" only for the two kinds that AREN'T this lane's own -- a planning lane also correctly excludes only ITSELF from "Move to Sprint Planning" while still offering any OTHER planning sprint as a target, verified live with two simultaneous planning sprints.
